The contracting authority intends to conduct negotiations with one or several tenderers. As a part of the competition, applicants shall deliver product samples (100 ml) by the application deadline. The product test is not included in the qualification evaluation and will not be used when assessing whether the applicant is qualified to participate in the competition. description-proc.eng: Fredrikstad and Sarpsborg municipalities invite tenderers to a dialogue conference to explore new initiatives to increase the work inclusion with input and ideas from different perspectives than those that tend to form the basis for procurements of labour market measures. The municipalities have a high proportion of non-Western immigrants and refugees among the population. NAV Fredrikstad and NAV Sarpsborg perceive that the existing measures are not sufficient for success well enough with work inclusion for this group. The offices are therefore working together on an innovative procurement with the aim of finding new initiatives that can contribute to the work including of non-Western immigrants with low education and language level. About the event Fredrikstad and Sarpsborg municipalities invite tenderers to a dialogue conference at Lisleby Samfunnshus, Monday 15 September 2025, 09:00-12:00. The target groups for the dialogue conference are suppliers, consortiums, nonprofit organisations or others who want to develop a comprehensive and innovative methodology for working including non-Western immigrants with low education and language level. NAV would like to explore new measures to increase the work inclusion with input and ideas from different perspectives than those that would like to form the basis for procurements of labour market measures. Suppliers who have worked on similar problems or have ideas they would like to try out are in the target group for this market dialogue. Fredrikstad and Sarpsborg municipalities would like to develop a methodology for increased work including where: • The target group shall have sufficient language to function in working life, minimum A2 level orally. • There shall be a focus on the individual ́s resources and interests. • The initiative safeguards the individual's overall need, based on the individual ́s social, economic and health situation. • The initiative shall have a work-oriented focus and aim of ensuring permanent work. • Models are developed that are different from the current existing tender for the target group. Programme for the dialogue conference. 9:00 Welcome and Introduction 09:10 The Challenge, Need and Assignment 09:30 Innovative procurements: the value of dialogue 09:45 What is an effect contract? 10:00 Break 10.15 Group Discussions 11:30 Information on the road ahead *Adjustments to the programme can occur. The three instruments of GET.pro are: - GET.invest mobilises private investments in clean energy by building a pipeline of bankable investment projects. - GET.transform supports partner governments by developing bankable frameworks for clean energy investment. - The Secretariat for Africa-EU Energy Program promotes strategic political dialogue between Africa and Europe on energy. Thematic and geographic scope: The implementation structure of GET.transform is organised along the Thematic and Geographic Approach. GET.transform offers structured advisory services on four key transformational topics: 1) Long-Term Energy Planning 2) Renewable Energy Grid Integration 3) On-Grid Regulation and Market Development 4) Off-Grid Regulation and Market Development On-Grid Regulation and Market Development measures enable power sector market reform allowing for renewable energy participation, increased investment, and promotion of private markets. Power system transformation processes should be supported by a background of technically sound energy planning, a well-functioning governance structure, policy and regulatory framework. The goal is to ensure that electricity resources, including generation, transmission, and distribution systems, are allocated efficiently. In addition, market model mechanisms can be designed and implemented to facilitate a sustainable, secure, competitive and affordable electricity system. To meet the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 target of universal access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services by 2030, decentralised renewable energy solutions such as off-grid solutions have been proven to be efficient at providing energy access to rural communities. Off-grid solutions can power over 400 million people across Africa and LAC. Off- Grid Regulation and Market Development establishes a framework for public partners to strengthen institutional capacities to accomplish their rural development mandates, as well as market incentives that promote private sector participation and finance for scaling projects. ? In addition to its core activities, GET.transform has implemented TA services to other GIZ- programs in Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as Asia and Europe. GET.transform is therefore offering activities potentially in all countries where GIZ energy portfolio is active by efficiently offering standardised solutions and scaling activities and contributing towards the concept of Vision 100 of GIZ, which serves as a guiding principle for the realignment of the GIZ portfolio for the global energy transition.

title-proc.eng: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: AI & Data Factory - Expert Services for AI and Data Development, Governance and Continuous Operations

description-proc.eng: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT AND MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the planned procurement is the acquisition of expert services for the establishment, development and operation of a centralized AI and Data Factory service (hereinafter the “AI & Data Factory”). The AI and Data Factory will support the Contracting Entity in developing, deploying, maintaining and continuously improving data, artificial intelligence, machine learning and analytics solutions and capabilities throughout their lifecycle. The AI and Data Factory service may include, but is not limited to, the following services: Decision Intelligence and Data Platform services Design, development, testing, deployment and continuous lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions, including business intelligence, data science, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI and agentic AI, as well as related data platform capabilities. The services may include, for example: - design and implementation of data, business intelligence, advanced analytics, machine-learning and AI solutions; - continuous development, maintenance, monitoring and lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions; - continuous validation and quality assurance, including model behaviour, outputs, end-result quality, data quality and data usage; - development, deployment and operation of AI and AI agent governance practices; - development, operation and continuous improvement of data platforms; and - other AI-, data-, analytics- and technology-related expert and consulting services supporting the objectives of the procurement. Data Governance and Management services Data governance and data management services may be provided as part of projects, continuous development activities and ongoing data management operations. The services may include, for example: - external data sourcing, data content development, data validation and data migration; - continuous data quality monitoring and improvement; and - development, implementation and follow-up of master data management processes for agreed data domains. The services are expected to be delivered in close collaboration with the Contracting Entity’s internal experts and other suppliers. The preliminary allocation of responsibilities between the Contracting Entity and the Supplier or Suppliers will be further specified based on the procurement preparation and market dialogue. The Contracting Entity intends to select 3 - 5 or more Suppliers. The final procurement and service delivery model, including the number of Suppliers and the allocation of responsibilities, will be determined during the preparation of the procurement. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The Contracting Authority seeks market input on the planned scope of the procurement, service model, preliminary service descriptions, procurement structure, competence requirements, commercial models and other elements relevant to the successful establishment and operation of the AI Factory. Suppliers are encouraged not only to comment on the Contracting Authority's preliminary proposals, but also to challenge the proposed approaches and suggest alternative, innovative or more effective solutions and operating models based on their experience, market practices and emerging AI capabilities. The Contracting Authority particularly welcomes ideas that may improve the scope, structure, flexibility, scalability, commercial model or long-term effectiveness of the procurement. The purpose of the market dialogue is to utilize market expertise in developing the procurement and to ensure that the final approach is feasible, proportionate, future-proof and aligned with market capabilities, while enabling innovation and the effective adoption of evolving AI technologies, services and operating models. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE - Market dialogue: H2/2026 - Publication of the Invitation to Tender: Q1/2026 - Evaluation of tenders: H1/2027 - Procurement decision: H1/2027 - Contract commencement: H1/2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a Prior Information Notice. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The Prior Information Notice includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest by email to tommi.aarnio@vr.fi no later than 28 September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize written consultation rounds, joint market dialogue sessions and, where considered appropriate, bilateral meetings with selected suppliers. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, timetable and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.

title-proc.eng: Global Employer of Record (EoR) Services

description-proc.eng: HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management Ltd (hereinafter "HAUS") invites tenders for the establishment of a framework agreement for Global Employer of Record (EoR) Services. HAUS implements international development cooperation, public sector reform and capacity-building projects in several countries worldwide. In countries where HAUS does not have a legal presence, local HR administration, payroll infrastructure or capacity to fulfil statutory employer obligations, HAUS requires Employer of Record (EoR) services to engage locally recruited personnel in compliance with applicable legislation. The purpose of this procurement is to establish a framework agreement with multiple service providers capable of providing compliant EoR services in a broad range of countries. Under the framework agreement, selected service providers will act as the legal employer of locally recruited staff while HAUS retains responsibility for recruitment decisions, work supervision and operational management. The EoR service shall include, at minimum: Legal employment of personnel in accordance with local labour legislation; Preparation and administration of employment contracts; Payroll processing and salary payments; Administration of statutory deductions, taxes and social security contributions; Benefits administration and mandatory insurance coverage; Onboarding and offboarding services; HR administration and local employee support; Compliance monitoring and reporting; Support related to work permits, visas and immigration matters when required; Provision or management of agreed work equipment where applicable. The services are currently required in countries including the Philippines, Moldova, Nigeria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Albania. In addition to these, future needs are foreseen in Nepal, Indonesia, Ethiopia and Tanzania. The list of countries is indicative only and may change during the framework agreement period. The procurement concerns the establishment of a framework agreement for Employer of Record (EoR) services for an initial contract period of 24 months. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to extend the framework agreement by two (2) optional periods of 12 months each (12 + 12 months). The maximum total duration of the framework agreement, including the optional periods, is 48 months (24 + 12 + 12). The purpose of the procurement is to select a maximum of three (3) service providers for the framework agreement. The selected service providers will deliver EoR services for locally recruited personnel in different countries, based on separate assignments issued during the framework agreement period. Individual assignments will be awarded later through mini-competitions between the selected framework agreement service providers. The framework agreement does not create any minimum purchase obligation for HAUS. The estimated maximum value of the framework agreement is EUR 8,000,000 (VAT 0%). The estimated value is not a commitment to purchase and does not guarantee any minimum volume of assignments. HAUS reserves the right to order services according to its actual needs throughout the framework agreement period. The procurement is intended for experienced international EoR service providers with proven capability to deliver employment, payroll, compliance and HR administration services across multiple jurisdictions, either directly or through legally compliant local entities and partner networks. A more detailed description of the procurement is provided in Annex 1 (TOR).

title-proc.eng: 10029875 - Consultancy services for strengthening the capacities of national and local actors for EU accession and alignment

description-proc.eng: The Republic of Moldova is undergoing an accelerated and complex European Union accession process following the opening of accession negotiations with the EU in 2024. The accession process requires comprehensive alignment of Moldova's legal, institutional and policy framework with the EU acquis, as well as strengthened governance structures, institutional coordination mechanisms and implementation capacities at national and local level. In September 2025, Moldova successfully completed the screening process for all chapters of the EU acquis, enabling the transition to structured technical negotiations and implementation of opening benchmarks and subsequent requirements identified during the screening process. These developments generate increasing demand for specialised expertise, institutional capacity development and practical support for the implementation of EU-related reforms. Particular importance is attached to reforms related to rule of law, democratic governance, public administration, justice and internal security, especially under Cluster I "Fundamentals", including Chapter 23 (Judiciary and Fundamental Rights) and Chapter 24 (Justice, Freedom and Security). At the same time, Moldova's EU accession process also requires stronger local governance capacities, improved multi-level coordination and increased participation of civil society, diaspora organisations and other stakeholders in EU-related reform processes. In this context, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH implements the projects "EU Integration Support Project" (EUISP), financed by the German Federal Foreign Office (FFO), and "Facilitating the EU Accession process through Coordination and Engagement in Moldova" (FACE), financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). To support the implementation of these projects, GIZ foresees the establishment of a comprehensive Short-Term Expert Pool (STEP), enabling flexible and demand-driven mobilisation of national and international expertise. The STEP will support activities related to legislative and policy approximation to the EU acquis, negotiation preparation and benchmark fulfilment, institutional and organisational capacity development, strategic planning and coordination, strengthening local governance capacities, facilitation of international cooperation and peer-to-peer exchange, as well as structured stakeholder engagement and support for local initiatives. The contractor implementing the STEP will provide technical advisory services, analytical support, capacity development measures, international exchange formats and implementation support in close cooperation with GIZ and Moldovan partner institutions. The overall objective is to strengthen the capacities of national and local actors to effectively coordinate, implement and support Moldova's EU accession and alignment process.

title-proc.eng: 10021232 - Supporting the Financial Institutions Green Transition

description-proc.eng: Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) constitute the overwhelming majority of economic activity in Jordan. MSMEs account for over 99% of all enterprises, employ around 60% of the formal private-sector workforce, and contribute 40% of Jordan Gross Domestic Product (GDP), making them crucial for economic growth, resilience, and job creation. Despite this importance, MSMEs still face obstacles in accessing appropriate and diversified financial products. Access to formal credit remains limited for many MSMEs. According to the Central Bank of Jordan (CBJ) National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) 2023-2028, only 28.3% of formal MSMEs had a loan or line of credit from a financial institution, highlighting a significant financing gap for smaller firms in Jordan. Financial exclusion is especially pronounced for underserved segments such as informal and women-led enterprises, which often face higher collateral requirements, limited credit histories, and lower formal borrowing rates. Financial inclusion, defined as access to and use of appropriate, affordable, and sustainable financial products and services, remains a priority in Jordan. The CBJ is pursuing ambitious targets to increase overall financial inclusion, reduce gender gaps, and enhance MSME access to finance, including through digital channels and tailored products. The NFIS aims, for example, to increase MSMEs access to formal lending at an average annual rate of 4% for four years. In a similar vein, Jordan"s Green Finance Strategy 2023-2028 aims to mobilize green investments and position the financial sector as a regional leader in sustainable finance. The strategy highlights that a 92.5% of the Jordan National Determined Contribution (NDC) target cost is to be financed by international support and mobilized private capital. As Jordan advances its Green Finance Strategy, a central priority was establishing clear and credible standards for what qualifies as "green" across the financial system. The Jordan National Green Taxonomy, published in February 2026, provides this clarity by offering a common language for the financial system to classify sustainable economic activities in a transparent and consistent way. By anchoring investment decisions to science-based criteria, the taxonomy helps ensure that future capital flows genuinely support Jordan"s low-carbon, climate-resilient transition. Against this backdrop, the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GIZ-implemented project, Innovative Approaches for the Financial Inclusion of MSMEs in Jordan (I-FIN), takes a holistic, market-driven approach to strengthening inclusive green finance in the country. The project operates across the policy, institutional, and market levels, helping to improve the broader enabling environment, upgrade the technical and operational capacities of financial service providers, and ensure that enterprises can confidently access and benefit from green finance solutions. The overall objective of the project is to ensure that MSMEs in Jordan benefit from a more inclusive financial system that enables inclusive access to green finance and supports environmentally sustainable and resilient business growth, also with a focus on women-led enterprises.

SPIRIT"s objective is to improve access to high-quality social protection services in Jordan for refugees and members of host communities with disabilities and their families, respectively. The main political partner of the SPIRIT project is the Ministry of Social Development (MoSD) of Jordan; the Higher Council for Persons with Disabilities (HCD) of Jordan is a key implementing partner. The key target group of the project are refugees with disabilities and members of host communities with disabilities and their families in Jordan, respectively. Mediators are social workers and MoSD personnel at the local level as well as technical staff and managers of the MoSD, the HCD and Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs). The project will work on four output areas. Output 1 aims to improve procedural requirements for the recognition of disabilities for both refugees and members of host communities. This includes supporting a test phase of the reformed procedure as well as its digital integration. The aim of Output 2 is to strengthen physical and digital referral mechanisms for people with disabilities. This includes the training of relevant staff in the application of standardised referral mechanisms as well as the provision of disability-specific services. Output 3 aims to strengthen decentralised MoSD institutions in Amman Governorate so that they can independently and systematically offer social services to support a self-determined life for people with disabilities and their relatives; particular attention is given to the needs of women and girls. Output 4 aims to provide relevant decision-makers with evidence-based guidance for the expansion of needs-based social protection services for refugees and Jordanians with disabilities; these recommendations are meant to adopted through national consultations and involving self-advocacy organisations. The project follows a multi-level approach. It aims to strengthen the institutional capacities of state agencies to provide social protection services for people with disabilities (organisational level) and to expand the individual skills of their employees (individual level). In the sense of an integrated approach, refugees and Jordanians are addressed equally. A gender-responsive design ensures that the needs of women and girls with disabilities are consistently taken into account and that family caregivers, mainly women and girls, are given targeted support.
